info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package kv is your key-value store: buckets of versioned values your apps read and write by key.

delete.summary: Removes one bucket of the caller's org — every key and every revision with it — and answers 204 with no body.
delete.description:
Removes one bucket of the caller's org — every key and every
revision with it — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the org has no
bucket of that name.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket's name, from the path.

post.summary: Creates a KV bucket and returns it.
post.description:
Creates a KV bucket and returns it. A bucket is keyed state on
the same durable plane as the streams: each key holds up to History
revisions, entries can expire by TTL, and watchers on the NATS port see every
write. 409 when the org already has a bucket of that name.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

delete.summary: Delete removes one key — a delete marker in the key's history, so watchers see it and Get answers 404 — and answers 204 with no body.
delete.description:
Delete removes one key — a delete marker in the key's history, so watchers
see it and Get answers 404 — and answers 204 with no body. 404 when the
bucket does not exist.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

get.summary: Get returns one key's current value and revision.
get.description:
Get returns one key's current value and revision. 404 when the bucket does
not exist, the key was never written, or its latest revision is a delete.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

put.summary: Put sets one key to one value and returns the revision the write created.
put.description:
Put sets one key to one value and returns the revision the write created.
Writes are versioned: each put is a new revision and the bucket retains up to
its History of them per key.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

get.summary: History returns one key's retained revisions, oldest first — every put and every delete marker up to the bucket's History depth.
get.description:
History returns one key's retained revisions, oldest first — every put and
every delete marker up to the bucket's History depth. 404 when the bucket
does not exist or the key was never written.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the key, from the path.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket's name within the org.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps.

ttl.description: TTL is the entry expiry in seconds; 0 means none.

values.description: Values is how many values the bucket holds right now.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps, 1–64. 0 means 1.

maxValue.description:
MaxValue caps one value's size in bytes. 0 or less means the server's
ceiling.

ttl.description: TTL expires entries after this many SECONDS. 0 means no expiry.

revision.description: Revision is the revision the write created.

created.description: Created is when this revision was written, RFC3339.

operation.description: Operation is what wrote the revision: put, del or purge.

revision.description: Revision is the entry's revision in the bucket.

value.description: Value is the value as UTF-8 text; empty for delete and purge markers.

data.description: Data are the key's retained revisions.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

value.description: Value is the value, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
